children: reported that drilling at Pelé South in Brazil returned high-grade shallow rare earth intercepts, including 6 metres at 13.2% total rare earth oxides from surface, extending a new exploration target near its Monte Alto project.

Pelé is part of the company’s broader Rocha da Rocha rare earths and critical minerals province in Bahia, where Monte Alto is the current anchor asset. BRE has been advancing a hub-and-spoke development concept across the province, with multiple deposits potentially feeding a planned central processing and separation hub at Camaçari.

BRE reported shallow intercepts from both ends of a priority corridor more than 2.5 kilometres long at Pelé South. In the south, auger hole STU2909 returned 6 metres at 13.2% TREO from surface, while STU2774 returned 6 metres at 11.4% TREO from 3 metres.

At the northern extension, the company reported 14.3 metres at 11.2% TREO from surface in diamond hole TG5DD0004 and 12 metres at 10.9% TREO from surface in auger hole STU1843. TREO stands for total rare earth oxides, the standard way rare earth grades are expressed.

Both southern holes ended in mineralisation, which BRE said supports follow-up work because the full thickness of the mineralised zone may not yet have been drilled. Even so, these intersections are exploration results, not a resource estimate.
Why it matters near Monte Alto

Monte Alto is BRE’s most advanced rare earth project and already carries a previously reported JORC resource of 4.4 million tonnes at 9.9% TREO. In its October resource update, the company said the total ultra-high-grade Monte Alto resource had risen to 4.40Mt at 9.87% TREO, with 3.54Mt at 10.71% TREO in the Indicated category.

Against that backdrop, BRE used Monte Alto as a reference point for Pelé South. Across 30 significant Pelé South auger intervals above 1% TREO, the company reported a length-weighted average grade of 5.0% TREO over 207 metres, compared with 2.3% for comparable Monte Alto intervals.

That comparison helps frame why Pelé has drawn attention, but it comes with an important limitation. The filing states clearly that the 5.0% figure is a selected-intercept average, not a deposit grade, so it should not be read as equivalent to a resource estimate.

BRE also reported a de-clustered TREO grade of 4.2% for those significant Pelé South auger intervals, plus a length-weighted scandium oxide grade of 203 parts per million. Scandium is another critical mineral sometimes found with rare earth systems, although the company has not outlined a standalone commercial case for it at Pelé.

The main gap in today’s result is continuity. BRE said only the ends of the corridor have been tested so far, leaving the intervening ground and two eastern geophysical corridors still requiring follow-up.

Assays are also pending for 44 Pelé South auger holes, which could change the geological picture in either direction. Diamond drilling is under way to test the underlying bedrock source, an important step because shallow auger results can indicate surface expression without proving the nature of the source rock below.

BRE said the next phase of work includes infill and extension drilling, bedrock testing, mineralogy and processing studies. Those studies matter because strong grades alone do not establish whether the material can be processed efficiently or integrated with the company’s existing development plans.

The wider project context also carries the usual development constraints for a pre-revenue explorer. BRE reported A$121.8 million in cash and cash equivalents at 30 September 2026 and no borrowings in its September quarterly, but the annual report states the company has no operating revenue and is likely to need additional financing as projects advance. Larger-scale development remains subject to feasibility work, approvals and funding.

The immediate question is not whether Pelé South has delivered eye-catching grades, but whether BRE can show those results connect into a continuous mineralised system. The next meaningful markers are the pending assays from 44 auger holes and the bedrock diamond drilling now under way, which should start to show whether Pelé is a standalone discovery or a more material feed option alongside Monte Alto.

title: Brazilian Rare Earths reports high-grade Pelé South intercepts
